more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
The EU rules checked in 2026 prohibit this additive in jelly mini-cups intended to be swallowed in a single bite; this is a restriction on that food format, not a ban on all authorised uses.
The EU rules checked in 2026 also prohibit its use in dehydrated foods intended to rehydrate on ingestion.
more_info.overview: Xanthan gum is a bacterial-fermentation polysaccharide containing glucose, mannose and glucuronic acid units. Its stabilising role is to help a food maintain its physical consistency or the distribution of its ingredients. Produced by fermenting carbohydrates with Xanthomonas campestris. The gum is recovered, purified, dried and milled. The specified material is supplied as cream-coloured powder. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.daily_intake: No numerical ADI needed for the assessed uses (EFSA, 2017).
more_info.origin: Produced by fermenting carbohydrates with Xanthomonas campestris. The gum is recovered, purified, dried and milled.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern for the assessed food uses.
At larger repeated oral intakes, some adults reported abdominal discomfort in short studies.
